text: 不要完全接受什么大数据推送给你的内容和观点，多想想，主动搜索一下有没有看着合理却完全相反的观点。
en: Don't fully accept whatever content and views big data pushes to you; think more, and proactively search for whether there are views that look reasonable yet completely opposite.

text: 说实话大数据推给我的真的是无力吐槽，看多了就觉得人工智能就是弱智，就好像我已经屯了大量便宜的卫生纸，你还给我继续不遗余力的推送更贵的更没有性价比的卫生纸。
en: Honestly, what big data pushes to me is really beyond complaint. After watching a lot, you feel artificial intelligence is just dumb — like I have already stockpiled lots of cheap toilet paper, yet you keep pushing me more expensive, worse-value toilet paper without sparing any effort.

text: 比如那种一个蠢货在台上拿着话筒对下面的信徒洗脑的视频我是看见一个拉黑一个。
en: For example, those videos of an idiot on stage holding a microphone brainwashing believers below — I block every one I see.

text: 什么xxx商业会，xxx商业思维，xxx经济学，我拉黑了有一年了，不下一百个账号，它还天天给我推，我是真找不到值得看的短视频了。
en: What xxx business associations, xxx business thinking, xxx economics — I have blocked for a year now, no fewer than a hundred accounts, yet it still pushes them to me every day. I really can't find short videos worth watching.

text: 你看那些大V吹嘘的大数据，人工智能就这副德行。
en: Look at the big data those big Vs boast about; artificial intelligence is just like this.

text: 那些所谓的互联网IT精英还以为短视频的成功是因为个性化推荐，呵呵！
en: Those so-called internet IT elites still think short videos succeeded because of personalised recommendations. Heh!

text: 看看你们这些蠢货都推荐了什么垃圾，只有屎吃并不意味着人们喜欢吃屎。
en: Look at what garbage you idiots have recommended. Having only shit to eat doesn't mean people like eating shit.

text: 很多人眼中的“信息茧房”根本就不是它实质的意思，而是觉得“互联网没有把最有用最精华的东西主动喂给我”。
en: The 'information cocoon' in many people's eyes is not at all its substantive meaning, but rather feeling that 'the internet hasn't actively fed me the most useful, most essential things'.

text: 大家都是成年人，别那么幼稚，干货要么是要钱的，要么是自己付出精力拆解出来的，哪来的自信认为这些东西必须要完全免费地送到你嘴里？
en: Everyone is an adult; don't be so naive. Dry goods (practical content) either cost money or are distilled by your own effort. Where does the confidence come from that these things must be delivered to your mouth completely free?

text: 实践就是最好的见识，没有之一，但问题是你也没实践啊。
en: Practice is the best insight — bar none. But the problem is you haven't practised either.

text: 说要养生，也没加班，作息却没改，早上依旧起不来。
en: Saying you want to stay healthy, yet not working overtime, your routine still hasn't changed, and you still can't get up in the morning.

text: 说要健身，也不忙，却连最简单的广播体操都懒得做。
en: Saying you want to exercise, yet not busy, but too lazy even to do the simplest radio calisthenics.

text: 所以“信息茧房”这东西就很魔性。
en: So this 'information cocoon' thing is quite demonic.

text: 有意愿行动的，自觉就会日积月累地提升基本功，自然而然地突破当下信息茧房。
en: Those willing to act will consciously accumulate basic skills day by day, naturally breaking through the current information cocoon.

text: 反而是想得多做得少的，只会沉浸在自己被信息茧房包围这样的焦虑情绪里，最多在对信息茧房热火朝天的理论探讨中偶尔得到一些兴奋情绪，现实并没有发生任何实质改变。
en: Conversely, those who think much and do little will only immerse themselves in anxiety about being surrounded by information cocoons, at most occasionally gaining some excitement in heated theoretical discussions about information cocoons, while reality hasn't changed substantively at all.

text: 别骗自己，就能解决大部分问题。
en: Don't lie to yourself, and most problems can be solved.

text: “信息茧房Information Cocoons”的核心在于：你被动接受信息的时长远远超过主动寻找信息的时长。
en: The core of 'information cocoons' (Information Cocoons) is: the time you passively receive information far exceeds the time you actively seek information.

text: 有一个通俗认知是：人们的信息领域会习惯性地被自己的兴趣所引导，这本无可厚非，但问题出在因果发生了些许变化。
en: There is a common understanding: people's information fields are habitually guided by their own interests, which is understandable in itself, but the problem is that cause and effect have shifted slightly.

text: Web 1.0时代，信息只读，没有CSS、动态链接、交互性，换句话说除了资讯门户网站（比如新浪网、搜狐网），普通网络用户没有机会发表观点，输出内容。
en: In the Web 1.0 era, information was read-only, with no CSS, dynamic links, or interactivity. In other words, apart from news portal websites (such as Sina and Sohu), ordinary internet users had no chance to express views or output content.

text: 这个阶段，网上冲浪连广告都基本遇不到，用户通过检索信息找到特定内容，信息接收的驱动机制来源于自己的兴趣。
en: At this stage, surfing the internet basically didn't even encounter advertisements; users found specific content by retrieving information, and the driving mechanism of information reception came from their own interests.

text: 过渡到Web 2.0时代后，可读可写的参与式社交网络诞生，大家可以在各种社区中分享他们的观点、意见、想法和经验，而为了促进广大用户多产生UGC，输出门槛不停下降，从博客（blog）到微博（microlog）到视频博客（vlog）再到图片博客（Plog），信息发布越来越直接，量级也逐渐攀升，知识密度与深度也变得稀薄。
en: After transitioning to the Web 2.0 era, read-write participatory social networks were born. Everyone could share their views, opinions, ideas and experiences in various communities, and to encourage users to produce more UGC, output thresholds kept falling — from blogs to microblogs to video blogs (vlogs) to picture blogs (Plogs). Information publication became more and more direct, volume gradually climbed, and knowledge density and depth became thin.

text: 滤镜美颜的图片，魔性洗脑的BGM，极易被共情的家长里短生活琐事填满了各个APP，平心而论，点一下确实无可厚非，但没有人可以逃脱奶头乐（tittytainment）带来的碎片信息成瘾。
en: Filter-beautified pictures, demonically brainwashing BGM, and highly relatable domestic trivia filled every app. Fairly speaking, clicking is understandable, but no one can escape fragmented-information addiction brought by tittytainment.

text: 慢慢的，时间消失，虽然看似读了很多内容，但实际上什么都没有获得，于是陷入极大的空虚感，后悔自己根本就不该点开第一条。
en: Slowly, time disappears. Although seemingly you read a lot of content, actually you gained nothing, falling into great emptiness, regretting that you shouldn't have clicked the first item at all.

text: 那么怎么改变这种信息链路呢？
en: So how to change this information chain?

text: 其实很简单。
en: Actually it's very simple.

text: 不需要卸载APP，不必对自己产生负罪感，而是把角色从一个被动接收者转化为输出者。
en: No need to uninstall apps, no need to feel guilty about yourself; instead, transform your role from a passive receiver into an outputter.

text: 信息输出需要大量摄入，而且是摄入深层次的知识，通过自己的阅读、理解、分析、转述，再利用这些APP，深入浅出的输出即可。
en: Information output requires large intake, and intake of deep knowledge — through your own reading, understanding, analysis, and retelling, then using these apps to output in a way that is simple and clear.

text: 举个例子，最近因为公司要求，我需要通过一个Power BI的考试，通过Microsoft的官方指导，我第一次发现微软自身提供了那么多丰富的学习资源，言简意赅，比很多需要付费的视频课程讲解的更通俗易懂，慢慢地结合题目我梳理了一个知识点合计，我就可以把这些内容通过自己的理解方式，再发到某个账号上，这个过程还应用了一遍费曼学习法。
en: For example, recently because my company required it, I needed to pass a Power BI exam. Through Microsoft's official guidance, I discovered for the first time that Microsoft itself provides so many rich learning resources, concise and clear, more accessible than many paid video courses. Slowly, combining the exam questions, I organised a summary of knowledge points, and I could then post this content through my own way of understanding to some account. This process also applied the Feynman learning technique once.

text: 其他的任何一种信息类型都可以采用这种方法。
en: Any other type of information can adopt this method.

text: 你喜欢电影，就不要去看那种5分钟说完一部电影的视频，去选择一部你感兴趣的类型片，静下心来从头到尾看完，然后去研究它的拍摄手法，剪辑技巧，剧本创作背景，演员演绎方式，配乐风格等等，在充分解构的过程中，你可以同步享受影片创作的精妙和美好，最后再结合读过的文字、看过的风景、自己的经历重构一篇影评，这种获得感与延迟满足会沉淀成自己的一部分，随着欣赏下一部电影迭代下去。
en: If you like films, don't watch those videos that explain a whole film in 5 minutes. Choose a genre film you are interested in, calm down and watch it from start to finish, then study its filming techniques, editing skills, script creation background, actors' performances, music style, etc. In the process of fully deconstructing, you can simultaneously enjoy the exquisite beauty of film creation, and finally combine words you have read, scenery you have seen, and your own experiences to reconstruct a film review. This sense of gain and delayed gratification will settle into a part of yourself, iterating as you appreciate the next film.

text: 当你养成这个习惯后，茧房早就不存在了。
en: When you develop this habit, the cocoon has long ceased to exist.

text: 我是凌十七Sapphire，一个在咨询行业摸爬滚打的小透明，时常点亮一些新的技能树。
en: I am Ling Shiqi Sapphire, a nobody fumbling along in the consulting industry, often lighting up new skill trees.

text: 欢迎关注我的公众号凌十七Sapphire来找我玩，和我一起在职场升级打怪吧^_^
en: Welcome to follow my official account Ling Shiqi Sapphire to come play with me, and level up and fight monsters in the workplace together ^_^

text: 现在信息获取渠道非常多，信息量也极大。
en: Now there are very many information channels, and the information volume is also huge.

text: 然而你所看到的都是已经被过滤筛选后的。
en: Yet what you see has already been filtered and screened.

text: 真实有效，敏感的信息不是在网上能看到的，同一件事，同一个对象也因为信息源的不同立场，会用捏造，扭曲，断章取义呈现出完全不同的形态。
en: Real, effective, sensitive information is not something you can see online. For the same matter, the same object, due to different stances of information sources, will be presented in completely different forms through fabrication, distortion, and quoting out of context.

text: 算法也会根据你的浏览喜好更把你禁锢在狭小的视野里。
en: Algorithms also confine you in a narrow field of vision according to your browsing preferences.

text: 提升自己的有效阅读量，建立知识储备。
en: Increase your effective reading volume and build knowledge reserves.

text: 培养提取信息，分析信息能力，不避开自己情感不喜欢不想相信的信息。
en: Cultivate the ability to extract and analyse information, not avoiding information your emotions dislike or don't want to believe.

text: 这样能从海量的垃圾信息里提取出更接近真相的东西。
en: This way you can extract things closer to the truth from massive garbage information.

text: 不要以为翻墙了就跳出信息茧房了，没有信息甄别，筛选能力的话，外网一样把你忽悠瘸。
en: Don't think that getting over the firewall means jumping out of the information cocoon; without information discrimination and filtering ability, the outside internet will dupe you just as badly.
